findings.title: NPE when the all-clients resource is missing
findings.body: In hasPermission(client, scope), if no per-client resource exists, getResourceTypeResource() is used. It returns null when the schema is not supported or the resource is absent. The next line, findByResource(server, resource), is then called with null, which can throw an NPE or give wrong results. A null check is needed before querying, and the method should return false in that case.

findings.title: Fallback to all-clients skips per-client negative permissions only when the resource is missing
findings.body: The per-client resource is looked up by client.getId(). If it exists, evaluation uses only that resource. It does not fall back to the all-clients permission. A client with a per-client permission for a different scope, such as VIEW only, therefore loses an all-clients MANAGE grant. This is inconsistent with the all-clients fallback used when no resource exists. The user-permission flow handles this differently.

findings.title: getClientsWithPermission uses findByType and includes the all-clients resource
findings.body: The resource for the type 'Clients' itself may be returned and its name ('Clients') added to the granted set of client IDs. Also, findByType may not match resources whose type is unset, because per-client resources are created without a type, so per-client grants may be missed. This makes listing unreliable.

findings.title: Dead code and unused imports
findings.body: getEvaluationContext is private and never used. The Logger, the TOKEN_EXCHANGE import, Scope and others are also unused. Remove them.

findings.title: Event listener gated on the V1 feature flag
findings.body: Cleanup of permissions on role, client and group removal is now gated by ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ. Previously it ran unconditionally. When only V2 is enabled, the listener stops cleaning up. When V2 is enabled, management() returns MgmtPermissionsV2, whose clients().setPermissionsEnabled now throws UnsupportedOperationException, which would otherwise break client deletion. The gating is a behavior change that is not explained in the description.

findings.title: canManageClientScopes and canManage() are inconsistent with the Javadoc for V2
findings.body: canView(ClientScopeModel) and canManage(ClientScopeModel) now grant access through the Clients resource type's permissions. The tests do not cover client-scope access. The tests also have no check that a MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE permission is enforced.
